shows: A shared appearance is treated as decisive.
example: Powders P and Q are both white, so they are one substance, beside: P dissolves 3 g and Q dissolves 25 g in 100 mL of water; look-alikes can differ.

error: Any mixing makes a new substance.
example: It vanished in the water, so it is a new substance, beside: Salt stirred into water vanishes, and drying the water brings the same salt back.
if_many: Day 10 follow-up, 10 minutes, after the day 2 repair: a separated mixture against a product with a different profile

example: Gas has no mass, beside: 0.8 g leaves a vessel and 0.8 g shows up at a collector.
if_many: Day 3 return and repair, 5 minutes, or day 6 warm-up: lay an open-cup record beside a closed-pouch record and ask where the mass went

error: Matter, or atoms, disappear during a change.
example: The chalk is gone, so the matter is gone, beside: The mass of everything inside the boundary is the same; the matter moved.
if_many: Day 3 return and repair or day 5 warm-up, 5 minutes: redraw one before-and-after card pair, counting particles in and out

error: Bubbles prove that a chemical reaction occurred.
shows: A state change or trapped gas is confused with a reaction.
example: Bubbles mean a reaction happened, beside: Cold tap water left in a warm room bubbles on the glass, and nothing new formed.
if_many: Day 4 warm-up, 5 minutes: sort four supplied bubble cases and ask what else you would compare

error: A closed reacting system loses total mass.
example: A closed system that makes gas loses mass, beside: The puffed pouch reads the same; the gas is inside.
if_many: Day 6 warm-up, 5 minutes: draw the boundary round pouch and gas, then count again

error: Crumbling proves that a chemical reaction occurred.
shows: Fragmentation is treated as a new substance forming.
example: It crumbled, so a reaction occurred, beside: Scraped fragments of the stone have the stone's own properties, so crumbling alone changed nothing.
if_many: Day 23 repair group for physical against chemical change: compare original and scraped-fragment properties

error: One matching property proves substance identity.
shows: A profile is reduced to one feature.
example: They match on one property, so they are the same, beside: Two liquids share a smell and differ in density.
if_many: Day 8 warm-up and day 12 warm-up, 5 minutes: compare two candidates that share only one property

error: Conserved matter means unchanged particle arrangements.
shows: Conservation is confused with unchanged substances.
example: The matter is conserved, so the particles must be unchanged, beside: The same atom cards can be regrouped into new particles with the same counts.
if_many: Day 23 conservation group: regroup a fixed collection of atom cards

error: Equal before-and-after mass identifies the gas.
shows: Boundary evidence is mistaken for identity evidence.
example: The readings match, so the gas is the same, beside: Two different gases in equal-mass closed cases read alike.
if_many: Day 7 warm-up, 5 minutes: two coded closed cases, equal mass, different gases; ask what else must be compared
